questions.prompt: A car travels 100 m in 20 s. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 100 m ÷ 20 s = 5 m/s.
questions.misconception: A loud option is 2000 m/s (multiplying instead of dividing); division — distance over time — is the correct relation.

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about speed?
options: It has a size but no direction
It always includes a compass direction
It can be negative when going backwards
questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar — size (like 30 km/h) with no direction attached, so it doesn't care which way you face.
questions.misconception: Speed swallowing direction is the hallmark of velocity, not speed. Negative speeds are a fiction — direction belongs to vectors.

questions.prompt: A cyclist covers 45 km in 1.5 h, stopping for lunch along the way. What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 45 km ÷ 1.5 h = 30 km/h, even though the rider surves faster between stops.
questions.misconception: Choosing 45 km/h ignores the time; choosing 67.5 multiplies. Average speed is the straight ratio of total distance to total time.

questions.prompt: On a distance-time graph the line is flat (horizontal). What does that tell about the object?
options: It is at rest — distance is not changing
questions.explanation: A flat line means no distance gained over time — speed is zero, the object is stopped.
questions.misconception: New learners sometimes read a flat line as 'big speed'; slope and steepness carry the speed, while flat means no climb.

questions.prompt: Two runners start together. Runner A's distance-time line is much steeper than Runner B's. Who is faster?
options: Runner A — steeper slope means more distance per second
Runner B — flatter slope means more distance
questions.explanation: A steeper distance-time slope means a larger distance gained in the same time, so Runner A is faster.
questions.misconception: A flatness = slowness mix-up is common; steeper slope always means bigger speed on a distance-time graph.
